title: PHP: out-of-memory request corruption
description: Unauthenticated requests can cause server-side code execution under vulnerable request-handling conditions. Assess every web-serving PHP installation.
affected: Web-serving PHP before the patched release in its branch; includes FPM, mod_php, CGI, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. Confirm vendor backports.
conditions: Older unsupported branches require a supported upgrade or a vendor-confirmed fix.
action: Update the PHP runtime and deployed images, restart all workers, and confirm the running web SAPI uses the fixed build. Temporary mitigations do not cover every attack path.

impact_scope.summary: The PHP security team identifies web-serving PHP installations across FPM, mod_php, CGI, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed as in scope. This spans applications using different server integrations; vulnerable versions and configurations still determine actual exposure. No deployed-server or affected-person count is published in this notice.

title: Node.js: Brotli decoder memory corruption
description: Processing attacker-controlled Brotli data can corrupt memory and permit code execution. Check services and dependencies that decompress untrusted content.
affected: Node.js 22.x / 24.x / 26.x before the October security release
action: Upgrade each deployed Node.js runtime to its patched branch release or a later supported release. Rebuild and redeploy images; verify the runtime inside running workloads.

title: Node.js: TLS hostname verification bypass
description: Non-canonical IP-like hostnames can bypass expected TLS identity checks. Review services making outbound HTTPS calls.
affected: Node.js 22.x / 24.x / 26.x before the October security release
action: Upgrade and restart affected clients; test certificate validation using normal application health checks.

title: GitLab: unauthenticated regex compiler RCE
description: A regex compiler integer overflow can allow unauthenticated server code execution. Prioritize self-managed instances.
affected: 7.0–18.11 before 18.11.13; 19.0 before .10; 19.1 before .9; 19.2 before .9; 19.3 before .6; 19.4 before .3; 19.5 before .1
conditions: GitLab.com is patched. GitLab Dedicated: verify the internal build against the vendor notice.
action: Use the supported GitLab upgrade path and patch immediately. Review the vendor detection guidance, worker crashes and anomalous rendering errors; investigate suspected compromise.

title: Compromised CA keys and root removal
description: Weak intermediate CA keys permit forged certificates against unprotected clients. Root removal can also break legitimate certificate chains.
affected: Clients with unpatched trust bundles; servers chaining to emSign ECC Root CA - G3
fixed: Updated browser/OS/runtime trust data; replace affected server chains
conditions: Chrome root removal is expected October 27, 2026 PDT; other trust stores have their own update mechanisms.
action: Update OS and application trust bundles, including containers and bundled runtimes. Replace affected server certificates through a trusted alternate hierarchy and test client connections.

impact_scope.summary: Compromised CA keys affect HTTPS trust across browser, operating-system and application trust stores that have not removed the affected CAs. Root removal can also interrupt legitimate websites using the affected certificate chain. The vendor describes protections for Chrome and Android; this does not mean all users remain exposed.
